claim: Worked example: a 50 C globe in 35 C air at 1 m/s sits in surroundings of MRT 74.8 C
law: Steady globe balance eps sigma (Tmrt^4 - Tg^4) = h (Tg - Ta), forced h = 6.3 v^0.6 / D^0.4 (ISO 7726 form)

claim: On a hot paved street in full sun the mean radiant temperature stays at or below 80 C
law: Stefan-Boltzmann with sphere view factors: ground 65 C, sky 25 C effective, 900 W/m2 direct and 120 W/m2 diffuse sun, absorptivity equal to emissivity

claim: The 150 mm black globe reaches about 67 C at 50 C air, MRT 80 C and 0.3 m/s
law: Globe balance solved for Tg with the larger of forced and natural convection coefficients

claim: Globe 90 % response is within 30 min (about 12 min with the probe bead)
law: Lumped capacitance tau = m c / (h A) of the copper shell; 90 % response 2.3 tau; the 10 mm bead adds a lag of about 4 min (CAL D5); conduction along the probe stem not included

claim: Psychrometric wet bulb of 35 C, 40 %RH air is 24.2 C
law: Stull (2011) empirical fit of psychrometric wet bulb, Pa 101.3 kPa

claim: With the fan the shield reads 0.43 C high in full sun at wind speeds of 1 m/s and more
law: Energy balance: every watt the plates absorb (3.74 W) could at most warm the 4.0 L/s fan flow by absorbed / (rho cp Q) = 0.79 C, above the 0.5 C target; the model value 0.43 C (HMN-CAL-001 C4) rests on assumed 50 % heat transfer to the air stream, a 2 s sensor lag and a 6 s fan run, and it gets worse below 0.5 m/s (independent review: SHT45 lag on a board under a cap may be 5 to 10 s, giving 0.6 to 0.75 C)
check: Plausible only: bound 0.79 C against the 0.5 C target; fan flow, sensor lag and plate-to-air coupling to measure (PR-001 now at risk)

claim: The 60 mm fan draws 4.0 L/s through the plate stack (60 % of its 6.6 L/s free-air rating)
law: Continuity: 1.6 m/s up the 56 mm column is 3.9 L/s; 14 CFM is 6.6 L/s; the stack's inlet area (110 mm x 12 mm gaps x 7) keeps the dynamic head near 1.5 Pa, far below a 60 mm fan's static pressure (class values, not a datasheet)
check: Fan curve of the chosen 60 mm fan against the stack not yet known

claim: A 35 m/s gust gives 750 Pa and 6.6 N on the globe
law: Dynamic pressure 0.5 rho v^2 = 750 Pa; drag on a sphere Cd 0.47 (subcritical)

claim: The arm stays below yield / 5 at a 35 m/s gust (wind 11 MPa, with the weight of the head 14.7 MPa, against the 110 MPa minimum yield)
law: Cantilever bending sigma = M / Z, 25 x 25 x 2 mm tube; wind and gravity bending added at the section corner (conservative); 6063-T5 minimum yield about 110 MPa (typical 145 MPa, stockist certificate to confirm); required factor 5; bolt holes at the root not checked

claim: The arm tube bends less than 10 mm at its tip at 20 m/s (tube bending only; rotation in the clamp and gravity sag not included)
law: Cantilever deflection F L^3 / (3 E I), E = 69 GPa, rigid root assumed

claim: Two strap bands at 1,000 N preload hold the arm against a twist of 18 N m (factor 2.5)
law: Band friction on the pole with the lined V: torque = n mu T r = 46 N m for mu 0.4 (FND-CAL-001); the preload and the rubber-on-pole friction are assumed

claim: The fan, run 6 s every 3 min, adds 35.3 mW of average load
law: Average power = P x duty / efficiency

claim: Sensors and fan (35.4 mW) stay inside FieldNode's 100 mW sensor allowance, so the 5.75 days without sun of FND-CAL-001 hold
law: Energy balance of the 3.2 V 6 Ah LiFePO4 cell (19.2 Wh) at the allowance, FND-CAL-001

claim: A 10 kOhm NTC (B 3950) reads 3.59 kOhm at 50 C
law: Beta equation R = R25 exp(B (1/T - 1/298.15))

claim: A 20 byte payload every 15 min costs 23.7 s of airtime a day at SF9
law: LoRa time on air (Semtech AN1200.13) with 13 bytes of LoRaWAN overhead, 125 kHz, CR 4/5

claim: One uplink (247 ms) is shorter than the 400 ms dwell limit on a US915 channel
law: FCC 47 CFR 15.247 and LoRa Alliance RP002 regional parameters (US902-928: 400 ms dwell, 125 kHz uplink channels)

claim: Reed-contact pull-up worst case is 0.109 mW
law: P = V^2 / R, 3.3 V across 100 kOhm

claim: The forced-convection globe coefficient 6.3 / sigma equals the ISO 7726 constant 1.1e8
law: Unit conversion between h (W/m2K) and the MRT form (K^4 per ...)

claim: Input errors add up to 0.30 C of WBGT as a root sum of squares of random terms (a warm shield bias of up to 0.43 C and a height bias of up to 0.4 C are one-sided and come on top)
law: Quadrature sum of the four contributions 0.23, 0.15, 0.09, 0.09 C; independence assumed, SHT45 typical figures, Liljegren model error not included

claim: Daytime urban heat island differences of 0.5 to 4 C (EPA: 1 to 7 F) can be seen with a node error of 0.43 C
law: Unit conversion 1 F = 0.556 C; two nodes with independent random errors of 0.43 C differ by 0.61 C in quadrature, so a single reading resolves a difference only at about 1.2 C (95 %%); a sunny site also reads up to 0.43 C warm against a shaded one
check: Fails for 0.5 C and 1 C; fix K2: restate the claim to differences of 2 C or more between single readings of sunny and shaded sites (the upper part of the EPA range; means over a season resolve smaller random differences but not the sun bias)

claim: After fix K2, differences of 2 C or more between single readings are resolved: 1.96 sigma of 0.61 C plus the 0.43 C sun bias
law: 95 % half-width of the difference of two independent 0.43 C random errors (1.96 x 0.61 C) plus the one-sided 0.43 C shield bias

claim: WBGT of 31.7 C follows from the formula 0.7 Tnwb + 0.2 Tg + 0.1 Ta
law: Arithmetic of ISO 7243:2017 (outdoors with solar load): 0.7 x 26.0 + 0.2 x 50 + 0.1 x 35; the 26.0 C wet bulb of the note applies emissivity 0.95 to the whole radiant load of a white wick and so reads high (conservative)

claim: 316 stainless fixings and bands in contact with 6063 and 5052 aluminium survive 10 years of weather
law: Galvanic couple of stainless steel on aluminium in a wet atmosphere: the aluminium is the anode and corrodes at the crevice; the cheeks, sleeves and saddle are separated from the stainless bolts by 8 mm aluminium crush sleeves and EPDM trim only in part
check: Corrosion at the bolt holes in salt air is not ruled out; sealant or plastic washers would reduce it

claim: White ASA plates, cowl and adapter blocks keep their shape and colour at the hottest shield temperature
law: ASA is a UV-stable ABS-family polymer with a glass transition near 100 C (supplier datasheets; the filament is not chosen); shield plates run about 15 to 25 K above air in the sun, so 65 to 75 C at 50 C air
check: Heat deflection temperature of the chosen filament to confirm

claim: The matte black globe paint holds its emissivity of about 0.95 as it ages
law: Matte black paints have emissivity of about 0.95 at the start; fading and dust change it over years

claim: The FieldNode LiFePO4 cell keeps charging in the shaded enclosure at 50 C air (57.2 C interior, FND-CAL-001)
law: LiFePO4 cells are usually specified to charge between 0 and 45 C and discharge to 60 C (cell datasheets vary); the interior of 57.2 C at 50 C air is above the usual charge limit
check: Fails in a heat wave: no charging above the limit and faster ageing; fix proposed to Amish and FieldNode (charge cut-off by cell temperature, HMN-DEC-001 O4, PR-016); not made here because the core belongs to the FieldNode repo

claim: WBGT, derived from the node's readings, is a screening index for heat strain, not a judgement on any one person
law: ISO 7243:2017 defines WBGT as a screening index; NIOSH (2016) criteria use it with work rate and acclimatization; the node reports environmental values only (planning and research data, not a heat warning)

claim: Wasps, spiders and dust do not block the shield gaps or the fan
law: Insects nest in sheltered gaps of radiation shields (a known field problem for naturally ventilated shields); 12 mm gaps, a fan every 3 min and a cowl lid reduce the risk
check: Field observation needed; inspection at each visit

claim: The Sensirion SHT45 holds +/-0.1 C and +/-1.0 %RH (typical) and survives 67 C in the shield
law: Sensirion SHT45 product page: typical +/-0.1 C and +/-1.0 %RH; operating range -40 to 125 C; typical values apply at 25 C, not over the whole range
check: Within the datasheet's stated typical figures; maximum values are wider

claim: The cup anemometer starts at about 0.8 m/s
law: Typical low-cost three-cup pulse anemometers start between 0.5 and 1 m/s (maker data, unit not chosen)
check: Start-up not measured; the calm share is reported and flagged

claim: The sensor head (without the FieldNode core) weighs under 4 kg: 2.11 kg in HMN-CAL-001 K1 (the D3 model of made and drawn parts sums to 1.60 kg without catalogue masses of bought parts)
law: Sum of component masses in sizing.py (volumes of the D3 model at each part's material density, bought parts at catalogue masses)

claim: [B] The 56 mm reservoir keeps the wick wet for 7 days at 45 C, 15 %RH, 1 m/s and MRT 80 C, with a 15 % headspace
law: Wick energy balance (sizing.tnwb) gives wet bulb 25.5 C and an evaporation flux of 0.48 g/m2 s over 7.5 cm2 of sleeve, 31.5 g a day if the worst case lasted 24 h; 7 days need 221 mL against 186 mL usable at an 85 % fill
check: Fails by 19 % in the extreme case; fix K1b: refill interval of 5 days in hot dry spells (158 mL) and 7 days otherwise

claim: [B] After fix K1b (the wick cord enclosed in a sleeve, so only the 7.5 cm2 sensor sleeve evaporates) the reservoir keeps the wick wet for 5 days at the same extreme
law: Same wick balance; 5 days at 31.5 g a day against 186 mL usable (margin 15 %, sensitive to wind: flux grows as v^0.47); an open 3 mm cord over the 0.12 m lift would add about 11 cm2 and more than double the use
check: Plausible: the sleeve must be sealed from the cord's neck to the sensor; delivery rate (S33) to measure

claim: [B] A cotton wick lifts water the 0.12 m from the reservoir surface to the sensor
law: Jurin's law h = 2 gamma cos(theta) / (rho g r) for 20 micrometre pores, gamma 0.072 N/m, complete wetting: 0.73 m static lift

claim: [B] The wick delivers water as fast as the sensor sleeve evaporates it (0.37 mg/s) at 1 m/s
law: Darcy flow through the 3 mm cotton cord needs the cord's permeability, which is not known here
check: Delivery rate to measure with the first wick

claim: [B] The reservoir bottle, filled to the brim, survives the water freezing at -20 C (R8)
law: Water expands 9.07 % on freezing; a brim-full bottle (3 % headspace) is split or its neck pushed off
check: Fails with 3 % headspace against 9.07 % expansion; fix K1: 85 % fill line and an invalid-below-5 C flag on the wet-bulb channel

claim: [B] After fix K1 the bottle survives the water freezing at -20 C: 85 % fill (15 % headspace) against 9.07 % expansion, a thin HDPE wall and a gland that is a loose push fit, so ice pushes it out
law: Water expands 9.07 % on freezing; headspace is necessary but not sufficient (ice forms first at the wall and neck and can trap liquid); the loose gland gives the ice a path; the invalid-below-5 C flag only protects the data
check: Plausible: freeze behaviour of the bottle to test at TRL 4

claim: [B] Distilled water and a clean wick keep the wet-bulb reading true for the visit interval
law: Evaporation concentrates dissolved salts on the wick and slows evaporation (the reason natural wet-bulb practice calls for distilled water and clean wicks); the interval is unknown
check: Wick life in street dust to measure; monthly visit assumed

claim: [B] A closed reservoir with a 6 mm gland breeds no mosquitoes or algae
law: Container mosquitoes lay in open water of a few centimetres; the cap has no open surface, only the sensor gland and a wick; light-tight dark HDPE limits algae; stagnant water in a closed bottle can still grow biofilm

claim: [B] The directly measured WBGT is within +/-1.0 C (R5): 0.7 x wick 0.5 C, 0.2 x globe 0.3 C, 0.1 x passive shield 1.04 C
law: Quadrature sum 0.37 C, linear sum 0.51 C; the 0.5 C wick error is assumed and is the largest term; wick fouling (S35) and non-standard wick geometry not included
check: Plausible: wick error to measure against a reference WBGT meter
